cohort: The study included all very low birth weight infants (<1500 g) with blood culture-positive candidiasis registered in a multicenter database of 70 Korean neonatal units between 2013 and 2017.
finding: Late-onset candidemia (LOC) was more common than early-onset candidemia (EOC) in very low birth weight infants, with LOC being associated with specific morbidities and longer treatment durations, and candidemia generally increasing mortality in extremely low birth weight infants.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was significantly more common in the late-onset candidemia group than in the early-onset candidemia group.
gest_age: Measured; significantly younger at EOC than at LOC for ELBW infants.
